lesson.title: Writing Linear Equations
intro: A linear equation can be written in point-slope form or slope-intercept form.
If two points are given, first find the slope using \(\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\).
Then substitute the slope and one point into the equation.

workedExample.problem: Write an equation of the line that passes through \((3,7)\) and has a slope of 2.
workedExample.aiHint: Use the given slope and point directly in point-slope form.

questions.prompt: What is an equation of the line that passes through \((3,7)\) and has a slope of 2?
questions.explanation: Use point-slope form \(y-y_1=m(x-x_1)\) with \((3,7)\) and slope 2 to get \(y-7=2(x-3)\).

questions.prompt: What is an equation of the line that passes through the points \((2,7)\) and \((-1,3)\)?
questions.explanation: The slope is \(\frac{7-3}{2-(-1)}=\frac{4}{3}\). Using point \((2,7)\) in point-slope form gives \(y-7=\frac{4}{3}(x-2)\).

questions.prompt: Which equation represents the line that passes through the points \((-1,8)\) and \((4,-2)\)?
